newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway debt closes gap with Bunds as crown gains.
newsitem.headline: Norway debt closes gap with Bunds as crown gains.

text.p: The Norwegian crown firmed following central bank announcement that it had lifted a self-imposed ban on intervention in the foreign exchange market in order to stabilise the currency.
Short rates were little affected but the long end out- performed Germany and closed the yield spread with Bunds.
Dealers said Norges Bank had given calming signal to market after recent fluctuations of the petrocurrency.
Bonds later followed international markets.
1400 GMT vs 1400 GMT on Monday
* 2007 bond yield two basis points higher at 5.93 pct
* Norway over Bunds gap four points narrower at 20 basis points
* Three-month eurokrone one basis point lower at 3.55 pct
* Crown 4.1850 against mark vs 4.2125
* Crown 102.86 vs inverse European Currency Unit index vs 103.53

The long end of the Norwegian debt market narrowed the yield spread with German Bunds following the central bank's announcement that it would begin interventions on the foreign exchange market in order to curb fluctuations in the crown.
The bank said it had decided to reverse a decision in January not to step into the currency market following a recent slide in the petrocurrency. Any intervention would be limited, it said.

"Norges Bank's transactions in the foreign exchange market have since January 10 1997 been confined to regular purchases of foreign exchange for the equivalent of about NOK 3 billion per month for the Government Petroleum Fund," the central bank said in a statement.

"In the light of developments in the foreign exchange market, Norges Bank no longer finds it appropriate to maintain special limitations on the use of instruments for the purpose of exchange rate management," it said.
The crown has weakened considerably recently, losing around two percent versus the ECU index since June 3.

Market players attributed the fall to higher-than-expected inflation figures for May, weaker oil prices and growing concerns over the outcome of parliamentary elections in September based on recent opinion polls.
The crown immediately rose on Tuesday and the yield gap with Bunds in the 10-year sector narrowed four points to 20 basis points. Debt yields later followed international movements.
"Everyone's watching the crown to see what happens now that Norges Bank has reversed its decision," said one dealer. "There's been very little in the bond market today."

Stein Bruun, senior analyst at Orkla Finans, said the bank had sent a calming signal to both forex and money markets. But it was too early to tell if the crown's recent fall was a fundamental shift in the exchange level.

"The pace and the size of the weakening has been concerning, but I think this was caused by a few sellers and a breaking of several technical levels. Foreigners are concerned about inflation and there's growing concern that the situation in parliament will be messy after the election.
"But on the other hand you have one of the best economies, there are not many countries with a budget surplus of six percent (of GDP) and a current account of seven percent," Bruun said.
--Tanya Pang, Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41
